family: disordered list of odd blocks of 1s split by single 0s
summary: The tape is (up to one or two runs) a disordered list of odd blocks of 1s separated by single 0s (11,687 blocks after 10^9 steps, lengths 1, 3, 5, ... with geometric-looking frequencies) that each sweep rewrites; open.
title: What is known about 1RB1RA_1LC0RF_1LD1LC_1LE0LB_0LF---_1RA1RB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RA_1LC0RF_1LD1LC_1LE0LB_0LF---_1RA1RB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is a list of odd blocks of 1s separated by single 0s, rewritten by each sweep in a way not yet understood.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 62,751 cells have been visited and 51,067 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.505).

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: For every length n of the run and any tape around it: L A> 1^n R reaches L 1^n A> R; L 1^n C> 1 R reaches L C> 1 1^n R. These are the moves the head makes across the long uniform stretches of the tape.

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: For every length n of the run and any tape around it: L A> 1^n R reaches L 1^n A> R; L 1^n C> 1 R reaches L C> 1 1^n R. These are the moves the head makes across the long uniform stretches of the tape.

claims.title: No periodic structure, no cellular-automaton rule
claims.text: Up to 3·10<sup>8</sup> steps the tape has no long periodic stretch, and no sliding-block code of radius up to 7 (with any fixed shift) maps the tape at one visit of the right end to the next on the last 400 sweeps.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts exactly when state E reads a 1.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine's tape is a long row of blocks of 1s, every block of odd length and every gap a single 0. Each sweep of the head rewrites the row, and the pattern looks disordered.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator.
Odd blocks of 1s on the tape at 10<sup>9</sup> steps, all gaps single 0s.
Crossing a block of 1s both ways, proved for every length.

sections.heading: Odd blocks, single gaps
html: Stop the simulator after the first few steps: every run of 0s inside the tape is a single 0 and every block of 1s has odd length, except for at most one or two runs (in 27 snapshots up to 109 steps), presumably where the sweep is at work. At step 109 there are 11,687 blocks:

The head sweeps across the whole tape and crosses each block with a simple shift rule (proved in Lean for every length), so all the changes happen at the single 0s between blocks. How a sweep transforms the list is the next thing to find; for now the order of the blocks looks disordered. The halt (state E reading a 1) needs a particular local pattern the sweeps have never produced.

sections.heading: Each sweep rewrites the whole tape
html: After 3·108 steps the tape is 33,829 cells of odd blocks of 1s split by single 0s, and it has no long repeated stretch anywhere. Every sweep of the head changes the whole of it, and not in a local way: no rule that computes each new cell from a window of up to 15 old cells explains the change. Information travels along the tape during a sweep, as when a number is multiplied digit by digit with carries. Finding that arithmetic is the next step.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.505).
After 109 steps the tape spans 62,751 cells (166 left of the start, 42,569 right), with a density of 1s of 0.814.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.
